Pages 7 through 9 detail the empirical validation of a MediaPipe and K-Means driven pipeline applied to fencing lunges. From a quantitative physics perspective, the athlete's body is a multi-joint mechanical linkage evolving in a high-dimensional configuration space $\mathcal{C}$. The 'reliability' mentioned in quote 2 corresponds to the stability of the projection map $\Pi: \mathcal{C} \rightarrow \{S_1, ..., S_K\}$ under perturbations. When the system performs best on standard lunges, it implies that the standard lunge occupies a deep, well-separated basin of attraction in the feature space, minimizing the gradient of the loss function near the centroid. However, the 'edge cases' represent regions of high curvature or topological folding where distinct tactical maneuvers (e.g., a feint vs. a commit) project onto overlapping clusters. This necessitates a refinement of the pose estimation manifold, likely requiring Riemannian metrics rather than simple Euclidean distances to preserve geodesic relationships between complex movements. Furthermore, the user satisfaction metrics (quotes 4, 7, 8) introduce a secondary, perceptual layer. The high usability score (4.6) suggests that the inverse problem—mapping cluster assignments back to intuitive visual feedback—is well-conditioned for the majority of the domain. Yet, the dip in visual design scores hints at a mismatch in the information density presented to the user, a classic signal-to-noise issue in human-computer interaction. Integrating these findings, we derive a composite sovereign primitive that not only classifies the pose but also dynamically adjusts the feedback bandwidth based on the local density of the pose cluster, ensuring that high-certainty classifications yield crisp directives while edge cases trigger expanded, probabilistic visualizations to maintain user trust and engagement.

The fencer operates on proprioceptive feedback and immediate tactical intent; the coach relies on holistic pattern recognition honed over years; the AI relies on statistical proximity in latent space. The 'clarity of feedback' metric essentially measures the alignment of the AI's internal representation with the coach's mental model. If the AI clusters a movement differently than the coach's implicit taxonomy, friction occurs. Therefore, the system must infer the coach's latent categorization schema to ensure the generated primitives are not just mathematically optimal, but pedagogically resonant.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the clustering granularity becomes too fine, leading to overfitting on noise rather than signal. If the intra-cluster variance drops below the sensor noise floor, the system will generate spurious corrections, eroding user trust. Conversely, if the clusters are too broad, tactical nuance is lost. We must enforce an anti-collinearity constraint between the pose estimation error and the clustering assignment confidence; if high pose uncertainty correlates strongly with cluster boundary crossings, the system must veto the automated feedback and defer to human oversight, preventing the propagation of hallucinated technical flaws.
